related_questions.question: Can I go to Canada with a US green card?

text_blocks.snippet: Yes, a U.S. green card holder can travel to Canada. U.S. permanent residents (green card holders) generally do not need a visa to enter Canada for visits. However, they must present a valid passport from their country of citizenship and their valid green card (or equivalent proof of U.S. permanent resident status) at the Canadian border.
snippet_highlighted_words: Yes, a U.S. green card holder can travel to Canada

list.snippet: Visa-Exempt: U.S. green card holders are visa-exempt for travel to Canada.
Required Documents: You must have a valid passport from your country of citizenship and your U.S. green card (or equivalent proof of status).
Entry Requirements: You will need to present these documents at the Canadian border when entering by air, land, or sea.
eTA: While not typically required for U.S. green card holders, if you are transiting through Canada to another country, you may need an eTA or visa depending on your nationality.
Criminal History: Be aware that a criminal record could affect your ability to enter Canada.

Consult an Expert: If you have any concerns about your specific situation, such as a criminal record or if you are unsure about eTA requirements, it's recommended to consult with an immigration lawyer or contact the Canadian Border Services Agency.

text_blocks.snippet: To travel to Canada from India, Indian citizens generally need a visitor visa, also known as a Temporary Resident Visa (TRV). This visa allows for temporary stays for tourism, business, or to visit family. Some reports say that the application process can be done online or through a Canadian visa application center.
snippet_highlighted_words: visitor visa, also known as a Temporary Resident Visa (TRV)

text_blocks.snippet: Here's a breakdown of the process and requirements:
1. Determine if you need a visa:

list.snippet: Most Indian citizens require a visitor visa to enter Canada.
If you're unsure, you can use the online tool on the Canada.ca website to check your eligibility for an Electronic Travel Authorization (eTA) instead of a visa.
Visitor Visa (Temporary Resident Visa - TRV): For tourism, business trips, or visiting family.
Work Permit: If you plan to work in Canada.
Study Permit: If you plan to study in Canada.
Super Visa: For parents and grandparents of Canadian citizens or permanent residents, allowing for extended stays.

list.title: Online Application:
list.snippet: The most common way to apply is through the Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) portal.

list.title: Application Centers:
list.snippet: You can also apply through a Canadian visa application center in India, such as VFS Global, which provides administrative support.
Valid passport with at least 6 months of validity remaining.
Completed application form.
Passport-sized photos.
Proof of financial support (bank statements, salary slips, etc.).
Travel itinerary (flight tickets, hotel bookings).
Letter of invitation (if applicable).
Biometric information (fingerprints and photo).
Proof of strong ties to your home country (job, family, assets).

list.title: Fees:
list.snippet: Visa application fees vary depending on the type of visa.
Purpose of Visit: Be clear about your reason for traveling to Canada.
Financial Stability: Demonstrate you have sufficient funds to support your stay.
Home Ties: Show that you have strong reasons to return to India after your visit.
Biometrics: Provide biometric information as part of the application process.
Processing Times: Processing times can vary, so apply well in advance of your intended travel date.
